feature: The Library in a video is a catalog grouped by kind
summary: With a video open, the Library has just Media and Catalog. The Catalog files titles, name cards, moving backgrounds, transitions and your pictures under chips with counts, keeps mockup components behind a Built for video checkbox, and adds any tile at the playhead with a double click or a drag onto the timeline.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Open a screen recording and turn on View > Library. Walk: video-library-catalog-walk.

try.do: Open a recording and choose View > Library. Look at the pivots: only Media and Catalog.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click Catalog, then the Backgrounds chip. Hover a tile to see it move.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click Title Pages and double click Keynote Clean, then Name Cards and double click Split Wipe.
Back on Backgrounds, double click Aurora, then drag Light Rays onto the timeline.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Untick Built for video and click the Components chip that appears.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Tick it again, pick Title Pages, and type cube in the search box.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Switch to a picture document's window: its Library still shows Media, Comps, Styles and Systems.

evaluate: Can you find a name card in one glance and one click, without scrolling?
Do chips above the tiles read better to you than a column down the side or a single dropdown (the open card on this task)?
Is Catalog the right word for the second pivot, or would something like Titles & More say it better?
Should a moving background land under the titles but over the recording, as it does now, or somewhere else?
Is it right that components only appear with Built for video unticked?
rough: How the kinds are picked (chips, a side column or a dropdown) is open on decision card in-a-video-the-library-is-a-catalog-of-things-bu-how-should-a-video-s-library-let; chips are built, matching the mock page video-library.html.
The shipped Library matches the mock page video-library.html (frames 1 to 4); the walk's video had no pictures, so its Logos & Brand chip is absent rather than different.
Animated Charts, Callouts and End Cards have no chip yet because nothing exists for them; charts arrive with task animated-charts-you-can-drop-into-a-video.

In a crowded dock (a clip picked, its Properties and Title sections open) the shelf shows about one row of tiles; whether the Library should be in a video's dock at all is the blocked task a-video-document-shows-the-library-in-its-dock.
Transitions now appear twice in a video's dock: the Transitions group and the catalog's Transitions chip. Both work; one of them may be one too many.

A moving background lands for five seconds on a Gfx track and covers the recording while it plays, which is what a background is for, but there is no way yet to pick its colours before it lands (it takes the title theme's palette).
A logo picked in the catalog opens the same section a Media picture does, whose button still says Place in Picture rather than adding at the playhead; double click and drag do add at the playhead.
